$comment: Shared CW decoder fixture, consumed by BOTH ports: android CwDecoderTest and ios MorseKitCheck. Data, not code — see CLAUDE.md's two-ports rule.

derivation.render: Hard-keyed CW as 16-bit PCM. unit = 1.2/wpm seconds; dit = unit, dah = 3*unit; gap after an element = unit, after a character = 3*unit, after a word = 7*unit, after the final character of the message = 10*unit. 0.7 s of silence leads (noise-floor calibration) and 0.5 s trails (flushes the last character). Each tone or gap spans trunc(seconds * sampleRate) samples. tone sample n = amplitude * sin(2*pi*toneHz/sampleRate * n), phase restarting at every element; gaps are silence.
derivation.noise: Uniform in [-noiseAmplitude, +noiseAmplitude), added to every sample including the silences, from xorshift64* (x ^= x>>12; x ^= x<<25; x ^= x>>27; out = x * 0x2545F4914F6CDD1D; a zero seed becomes 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15): value = ((out >> 40) / 8388608 - 1) * noiseAmplitude. A noiseAmplitude of 0 adds nothing and does not advance the generator.
derivation.sample: clamp(value + noise, -32767, 32767) truncated toward zero to Int16.
derivation.decode: The core's default config with input_rate_hz = inputRate and target_rate_hz = 8000; every on_symbol text appended in order and whitespace-trimmed. passes > 1 replays the same PCM after a decoder reset with the sink cleared, and the pass outputs are joined with '|'.
derivation.expectations: expectedText is the message itself (the spec), repeated per pass. wpmRange and expectedToneHz/toneToleranceHz are the documented tolerances of the core's speed and pitch estimators, not measured values.
derivation.renderedSamples: Exact: every segment length is integer arithmetic on the same doubles both ports use.
derivation.absSum: Sum of |sample| over the whole render. Computed here in double precision with a correctly-rounded sin; the ports truncate the same doubles, so a flip needs a sample within one ulp of an integer boundary — which is why the relative tolerance is loose next to the exact count. A real regression in either renderer (a wrong gap, a dropped element, unseeded noise) moves this by percent.
derivation.note: Re-implemented from this description, not transcribed from either port. It pins both bench renderers to the same audio and the vendored core to the same copy of it; it is not a claim about the core's accuracy against any external standard.

cases.name: clean 25 WPM at 700 Hz (8 kHz PCM)
cases.message: CQ CQ DE N9HO N9HO K
cases.expectedText: CQ CQ DE N9HO N9HO K
cases.note: the baseline: hard-keyed CW at the core's default pitch, decoded at its native rate

cases.name: pitch search recovers a 620 Hz signal against the 700 Hz default
cases.message: CQ CQ DE N9HO N9HO K
cases.expectedText: CQ CQ DE N9HO N9HO K
cases.note: 80 Hz off the seed pitch, inside the 500-900 Hz search window

cases.name: stays solid through seeded noise (~20 dB SNR)
cases.message: CQ CQ DE N9HO N9HO K
cases.expectedText: CQ CQ DE N9HO N9HO K
cases.note: uniform noise at 1/8 of the tone amplitude is ~20 dB SNR by power, far inside the ~11 dB limit measured for this core, so the case stays deterministic across toolchains and math libraries

cases.name: 48 kHz input decimates down and still decodes
cases.note: the rate a phone microphone delivers; the core decimates to targetRate before detecting

cases.name: reset() rearms the decoder for a second run
cases.note: the same PCM twice with a reset between; both passes must copy cleanly
